silicon.0x0: Software end: after NBYTES are transferred (the last byte ACKed on a write, the last byte received on a read) TC is set and SCL is stretched; no STOP until software sets STOP or START (p2004, p2011).
silicon.0x1: Automatic end: after NBYTES are transferred a STOP is sent and STOPF is set; TC is not set (p2004, p2011, p1979).

twin.0x0: The guard forwards CR2 unchanged; the stock model sets TC at once when the NBYTES-th TXDR byte is written (write) or when the last byte is read out of RXDR (read), with no bus time; no STOPF.
twin.0x1: The stock model sets STOPF (and leaves controller mode) at the same instants; TC not set. A NACKed address's STOP is the guard's, whatever AUTOEND.

differs: Timing only, for both values: the twin raises TC (0) or STOPF (1) at the instant of the last TXDR write, or of the last RXDR read, with no bus time; silicon raises it when the last byte has been transferred on the bus (for a read, when the byte is received, before software reads it). A firmware that polls sees the completion flag on its first read. (With RELOAD = 1 the stock model would also set STOPF where p2004 says AUTOEND has no effect; RELOAD is never 1 in any write here.)
observable_by_firmware: By polling I2C_ISR. The generated boots poll it at the CPU's pace (genlog/hse-crystal-16 console, i2c1 at 0.000033290): after TXDR 0xD0 (AUTOEND = 0, NBYTES = 1) the very next ISR read returns 0x41 (TC set); after the AUTOEND = 1 read START 0x20124EC the next reads return 0x5 (RXNE), then 0x21 (STOPF) right after the RXDR read, all in one virtual instant. On silicon those reads fall inside the byte's nine SCL periods (and the STOP after it) and return TC = 0 / RXNE = 0 / STOPF = 0. ArduPilot (armed run) takes the flags in its interrupt, about 1 us after the write (TXDR 0.185047990, ISR 0x41 0.185048970).
notes: The I2C bus takes no time in the stock model for any field; this row counts it because AUTOEND's own effect (TC vs STOP) is that timed event. AUTOEND = 1 with RELOAD = 1 (stock L442-450 sets both STOPF and TCR) differs from p2004 but no write has RELOAD = 1 (all_values covers AUTOEND, not RELOAD). Generated i2c1 ISR reads of 0x31 (STOPF|NACKF|TXE) are the guard's NACK model, not AUTOEND.

silicon.any byte: The byte is shifted onto the bus after the address; TXE and TXIS clear at the write and set again after the ninth SCL pulse with an ACK (p2011, p1975).

twin.any byte: With PE = 1 and an open write transfer the guard forwards the word; the stock model queues the byte and hands the device all NBYTES bytes at once when the last is written, TXE always reads 1, and TXIS stays 1 until the last byte (then TC or STOPF at once). With PE = 0 or outside a write data phase it refuses (TVI-I2C-TRANSFER).

differs: Flags and timing around each write, for every byte: TXE reads 1 always (silicon 0 from the write until the byte moves to the shift register), TXIS stays 1 between the bytes of a multi-byte write (silicon clears it at each write and sets it after the byte's ACK), and the device receives the bytes only when the NBYTES-th is written, with no bus time. The byte values reaching the device are the same.
observable_by_firmware: By reading I2C_ISR between a TXDR write and the byte's transmission. The generated boots do: genlog/hse-crystal-16 console, i2c1 at 0.000042090: START 0x203208C (NBYTES = 3), ISR 0x3, TXDR 0x36, ISR 0x3 (TXIS and TXE still 1) at the same virtual instant, where silicon returns TXIS = 0 and TXE = 0 until the byte has gone (p2011, p1975); after a single-byte TXDR (0xD0, 0x1) the next read is 0x41 (TC) at once (also sentinel-03 at 0.000060520). The armed run reads ISR only in the interrupt the twin's TC raises (0x41 about 1 us after the write).
notes: ArduPilot's TXDR writes are CPU word writes (1455 in the armed run). TXDR bit 8 is a gap in the stock register (fields 0-7, reserved 9-31). Silicon's TXDR is written 'only when TXE = 1'; the twin's TXE is always 1, so no write is ever early by that test.
